title: Competitive scouting playbook and experiment lab for rapid model landscape signals
creator: Priya Patel
description: Create a repeatable playbook and lightweight experiment lab that harvests, normalizes, and surfaces competitive signals about open and hosted models. The goal is to deliver weekly snapshots that combine capability probes, availability/latency telemetry, pricing changes, and vendor release notes into a ranked signal feed for PMs and sourcing. This ticket covers the PM work: probe definitions, success metrics, dashboard spec, sampling cadence, cost guardrails, experiment plan, and handoff to analytics/infra for automation.
acceptance_criteria: Probe spec doc that defines 12 rapid probes (NLP/cloze, summarization, RAG sanity, hallucination check, embeddings stability, latency/95th perc distribution) and expected success signals
Weekly snapshot pipeline: ingest from 3-4 model endpoints, normalize outputs, compute delta metrics vs previous snapshot
Dashboard spec with model-ranking view, signal timeline, and alerting thresholds documented and reviewed
Cost & sampling policy: budget guardrail defined and approved by finance and infra
Operational runbook for false-positive handling and escalation to sourcing or applied-ML
success_metrics: Time-to-action: median time from new adverse signal (drift/outage/price spike) to PM acknowledgment < 24h
Signal precision: > 80% of high-priority alerts validated as real by analyst sampling
Coverage: weekly snapshots include at least 85% of models on the watchlist for the targeted verticals
Cost efficiency: probe-run cost per snapshot stays under $350 for the baseline watchlist
notes: Design choice: start narrow (10-15 models) and expand — wide coverage is expensive and noisy
Trade-offs: end-to-end automation requires infra work; initial phase will be semi-automated with CSV drops to accelerate delivery
Privacy: do not send customer data to probes; use synthetic prompts and public-domain evaluation corpora
Data retention: keep snapshots for 90 days in the initial phase to allow short-term trend analysis
Stakeholders: PMs (market intel), Applied ML (probe design), Analytics (pipeline), Infra (credentials/endpoints), Finance (budget)
